classic-nlp.prompt: In TF-IDF, which words get the highest weight in a document?
classic-nlp.explanation: tf⋅log⁡(N/df)\text{tf}\cdot\log(N/\text{df})tf⋅log(N/df): high term frequency and high inverse document frequency.
options: Words frequent in this document but rare across the corpus

classic-nlp.prompt: A term appears in 10 of 1,000 documents. What is its IDF with natural log, ln⁡(N/df)\ln(N/\text{df})ln(N/df)? (two decimals)
classic-nlp.explanation: ln⁡(100)≈4.61\ln(100)\approx4.61ln(100)≈4.61.

classic-nlp.prompt: Perplexity of a language model is…
classic-nlp.explanation: Lower perplexity means the model is less surprised by the test text.
options: the exponential of the average negative log-likelihood per token

classic-nlp.prompt: TF-IDF with logistic regression is still a strong baseline for text classification.
classic-nlp.explanation: It is fast, interpretable and often within a few points of fine-tuned models on topic and sentiment tasks.

word-embeddings.prompt: What problem does negative sampling solve in word2vec?
word-embeddings.explanation: It replaces the full softmax with a few binary "real vs noise" comparisons per example.
options: The softmax denominator over the whole vocabulary is too expensive

word-embeddings.prompt: Which limitation do static word embeddings have that contextual embeddings fix?
word-embeddings.explanation: Contextual models give each occurrence its own vector depending on the sentence.
options: One vector per word, so "bank" (river) and "bank" (money) share a vector
They cannot be trained on GPUs

word-embeddings.prompt: In embedding space, vking−vman+vwoman\mathbf v_{\text{king}}-\mathbf v_{\text{man}}+\mathbf v_{\text{woman}}vking​−vman​+vwoman​ lands near which word?
word-embeddings.explanation: Relationships such as gender are approximately consistent directions in the space.

tokenization.prompt: What does each step of byte-pair encoding training do?
tokenization.explanation: Repeating the merge builds a vocabulary of frequent subwords up to the target size.
options: Splits the longest word in half
Merges the most frequent adjacent pair of symbols into a new symbol

tokenization.prompt: Why do byte-level tokenizers start from the 256 byte values?
tokenization.explanation: Every string is a sequence of bytes, so coverage is guaranteed.
options: Any text in any script can be encoded, so there is no unknown token
It makes the vocabulary smaller than 256

tokenization.prompt: Languages underrepresented in tokenizer training typically need more tokens per word. Which consequences follow? (select all)
tokenization.explanation: Token count drives cost, context use and latency.
options: Higher API cost for the same text
Less text fits in the context window

pretrained-nlp.prompt: Which model family is pretrained with masked language modelling?
pretrained-nlp.explanation: BERT hides about 15% of input tokens and predicts them from both sides.

pretrained-nlp.prompt: Which is the best fit for named-entity recognition on a new domain with a few thousand labelled sentences?
pretrained-nlp.explanation: Token-level heads on contextual embeddings are the standard, data-efficient approach.
options: Fine-tuning a pretrained encoder with a token-classification head

pretrained-nlp.prompt: A typical learning rate for fine-tuning BERT-sized encoders is around…
pretrained-nlp.explanation: Small rates preserve the pretrained knowledge; a few epochs usually suffice.

speech.prompt: What input representation do most speech models use?
speech.explanation: Short-time Fourier transforms mapped to the mel scale and log-compressed.

speech.prompt: What problem does CTC loss solve?
speech.explanation: CTC sums the probability of every frame-level path that collapses to the target.
options: The unknown alignment between many audio frames and fewer output characters

speech.prompt: A reference has 10 words; the hypothesis has 1 substitution, 1 deletion and 1 insertion. What is the WER?
speech.explanation: (S+D+I)/N=3/10(S+D+I)/N=3/10(S+D+I)/N=3/10.

info-extraction.prompt: In BIO tagging, what does B-ORG mark?
info-extraction.explanation: B begins an entity, I continues it, O is outside.
options: The first token of an organization name
The last token of an organization

info-extraction.prompt: Why add a CRF layer on top of a BERT encoder for NER?
info-extraction.explanation: Learned transition scores plus Viterbi decoding give consistent sequences.
options: To score whole tag sequences and avoid invalid transitions like O → I-ORG

info-extraction.prompt: What is the time complexity of Viterbi decoding for T tokens and K tags?
info-extraction.explanation: Dynamic programming considers every previous tag for every current tag at each step.

info-extraction.prompt: When extracting fields with an LLM, which practices matter? (select all)
info-extraction.explanation: LLMs can return confident but wrong values.
options: Validate the output against a JSON schema
Measure field-level accuracy on a labelled sample
Route low-confidence or invalid cases to a human
Trust the output because it looks plausible

arabic-nlp.prompt: Which normalization steps are common for Arabic search? (select all)
arabic-nlp.explanation: These remove spelling variation that carries little meaning for retrieval.
options: Unifying alef variants (أ إ آ → ا)

arabic-nlp.prompt: In Arabizi, which digit usually stands for the letter ع?
arabic-nlp.explanation: Arabizi uses digits that look like Arabic letters: 3 for ع, 7 for ح, 9 for ق.

arabic-nlp.prompt: Why are character n-grams effective for dialects like Darija?
arabic-nlp.explanation: Word-level features would see each spelling as unrelated.
options: Unstandardized spellings of the same word still share many character n-grams

arabic-nlp.prompt: An English-centric tokenizer usually splits Arabic into more tokens per word than English.
arabic-nlp.explanation: That raises cost and shortens the effective context; measure it on your data.

__exam.prompt: You need sentence embeddings for semantic search in Arabic, French and English. What should you use?
__exam.explanation: Multilingual embedders map meaning across languages into one space; quality varies, so evaluate per language.
options: A multilingual sentence-embedding model, checked on your own queries per language

__exam.prompt: Which pairs are correctly matched? (select all)
__exam.explanation: word2vec gives one static vector per word.

__exam.prompt: A model gets 90% accuracy on MSA test data but 60% on Darija comments. What should you do first?
__exam.explanation: Averages hide failing segments; dialect data closes the gap.
options: Collect and label in-domain dialect data, then evaluate and fine-tune per segment

__exam.prompt: What is the WER if the hypothesis has 2 substitutions and 2 deletions against a 20-word reference?
__exam.explanation: (2+2+0)/20=0.2(2+2+0)/20=0.2(2+2+0)/20=0.2.
